evidence_type: direct assay (in organello import) + mutant phenotype
claim_tested: Tom20, Tom70, Tom22 are MIM clients
key_finding: Mim1 required for insertion and assembly of Tom20 and Tom70 but NOT Tom22
context: S. cerevisiae isolated mitochondria, mim1 mutant, BN-PAGE
confidence_and_limitations: High for Tom20/Tom70; the Tom22 negative is explicit and has never been retracted. Seed hypothesis lists Tom22 as a client, which is wrong.

evidence_type: direct assay (Fis1-specific insertion assay) + liposome reconstitution
key_finding: None of the known OM import components affected Fis1 steady-state levels or in vitro insertion; Fis1 inserted into protein-free vesicles; ergosterol inhibited
confidence_and_limitations: High. Pre-dates Mim2 discovery, so a residual MIM-complex contribution was not formally excluded, but mim1 was tested.

claim_tested: A dedicated insertase exists for MOM tail-anchored proteins
key_finding: No mutant in the whole-genome deletion collection blocked insertion; ergosterol content of the target membrane determines specificity
context: S. cerevisiae, model MOM TA reporters
confidence_and_limitations: High for the absence of an obligate insertase for this reporter class; reporters may not represent all TA proteins.

stance: competing / supports a broader client set
claim_tested: MIM is restricted to multispan proteins
key_finding: MIM promotes insertion of both signal-anchored and tail-anchored single-spanning proteins; MIM exists in three populations (TOM-bound, free, SAM-coupled)
confidence_and_limitations: Medium for this analysis: abstract states the class but no open-access full text was retrievable (not in Europe PMC or PMC), so the exact per-protein substrate list could not be verified here.

evidence_type: specific in vitro insertion assay + native PAGE
key_finding: Mim1 central for Ugo1 insertion; Tom70 recognises the precursor; TOM pore not required
confidence_and_limitations: High. Ugo1 is one of the two proteins the hydrophobicity rule misclassifies.

key_finding: mim1 mitochondria impaired in biogenesis of multispanning OMM proteins; Mim1 overexpression stimulates import; MIM cooperates with Tom70

claim_tested: Tom6 and Tom22 use the same route
key_finding: Tom6 is inserted in an Mim1-dependent manner then bound by SAM-Tom5/Tom40; Tom22 is handled by SAM-Mdm10
confidence_and_limitations: High. Independently confirms the Tom22 negative.

key_finding: mim1 mitochondria phenocopy tom5 at SAM stage 2; Mim1's effect on Tom40 is largely via Tom5 import
confidence_and_limitations: Medium-high; Tom5 dependence is inferred from an epistasis-style argument.

claim_tested: Mim2 is part of, and depends on, the MIM complex
key_finding: Mim2 interacts physically and genetically with Mim1; mim2 cells have lower steady-state levels of helical MOM proteins
confidence_and_limitations: High for the complex; Mim2's own biogenesis dependence is partly self-referential.

key_finding: Om45 import occurs via TOM and the TIM23 presequence translocase; assembly in the OM involves the MIM machinery
confidence_and_limitations: Medium. 'Assembly involves' is weaker than 'insertion requires'.

key_finding: Om45 import requires Tom20, Tom22, Tom40, the TIM23 complex and membrane potential; no MIM requirement reported
confidence_and_limitations: Medium-high. Same year, same protein, different conclusion from PMID:24781695.

key_finding: Recombinant Om45 and its signal-anchor peptide associate with mitochondria without cytosolic factors; peptide adopts TM topology in bilayers; prefers OMM-like lipids
confidence_and_limitations: Medium. In vitro only; does not exclude a MIM contribution in vivo.

key_finding: For Om14, Mim1 and porin support optimal membrane integration but neither is absolutely required; unfolding, hydrophobicity and membrane fluidity all contribute
confidence_and_limitations: High. Shows MIM dependence is quantitative, which undermines a binary classification rule.

key_finding: Mim1's own biogenesis uses Tom70 and the cytosolic co-chaperone Djp1; GFP-Mim1 mislocalises to ER in djp1
confidence_and_limitations: High. Means Mim1 in the MIM-independent class is a special, self-referential case.

evidence_type: in vivo, in organello and in vitro peptide binding
claim_tested: Anchor hydrophobicity alone determines the route
key_finding: Hsp70/Hsp90 and Hsp40 co-chaperones Ydj1/Sis1 bind newly made signal-anchored proteins through their hydrophobic TM segments before handover to Tom70
confidence_and_limitations: High. Adds a cytosolic triage step upstream of MIM that a sequence-only rule cannot capture.

claim_tested: A single biophysical parameter assigns the insertion route
key_finding: Targeting is organised by substrate TOPOLOGY, not by a scalar hydrophobicity: NAC for polytopic, TTC1 for signal-anchored
confidence_and_limitations: High for mammals; the yeast MIM has no mammalian ortholog, so transfer is indirect. Supports topology as the governing variable.

claim_tested: MIM recognises a conserved sequence signature
key_finding: Trypanosome pATOM36, with no sequence or topological similarity to Mim1/Mim2, fully substitutes for the MIM complex in yeast and vice versa
confidence_and_limitations: High. Convergent insertases with unrelated sequences performing the same task argue against a precise sequence-encoded client code.

claim_tested: Client selection is encoded in a yeast-specific recognition motif
key_finding: Human MTCH1, evolutionarily unrelated to Mim1, restores biogenesis of MIM substrates, TOM stability and mitochondrial morphology in yeast lacking the MIM complex
confidence_and_limitations: High. Reinforces that substrate selection is generic insertase chemistry rather than a specific recognition rule.

claim_tested: Any single anchor parameter separates MIM-dependent from MIM-independent proteins
key_finding: Best parameter mean GES hydrophobicity: AUROC 0.933, raw p=0.028, FDR p=0.246 over 16 parameters; threshold rule balanced accuracy 0.900 but permutation p=0.069; misclassifies Ugo1 and Scm4; signal lives entirely in the annotated anchor EDGES (AUROC 0.933) not the core (0.667) and falls to AUROC 0.767 with a boundary-free anchor definition
context: UniProt S. cerevisiae sequences, n=10 MIM-dependent vs n=3 MIM-independent
confidence_and_limitations: Low-medium. Negative class has only 2-3 members, which caps the attainable p-value; anchor boundaries are themselves predictions.
